source_text: Πατέρα, εἰ μὴ δι' ἐμοῦ.» Πλὴν εἰ καὶ γέγονε καθ' ἡμᾶς, καθιεὶς ἑαυτὸν εἰς ἀνθρωπότητά τε καὶ κένωσιν ὁ μονογενὴς τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος, ἀλλ' ἔστι καὶ ἴδιον αὐτοῦ φυσικῶς τὸ ἐν δόξῃ νοεῖσθαι τῇ θεοπρεπεῖ, καὶ ἐν ὑπεροχαῖς ὑπάρχειν ταῖς ὑπὲρ τὴν κτίσιν, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ πρὸ τῆς σαρκός. Διὰ τοῦτο τὰ Χερουβὶμ περιεστᾶσι τὸ ἱλαστήριον, πυκάζοντα ταῖς πτέρυξι, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸ τετραμμένα, καὶ ἀεὶ τὸ πρόσωπον ἐπερείδοντα, καὶ δορυφορίας μὲν ἀπόδειξις ἐναργὴς, ἡ εἰς δεξιά τε καὶ εὐώνυμα στάσις. Τὸ δὲ τῶν ἀνωτάτω δυνάμεων οἱονεί πως ἔντονόν τε καὶ ἀκόρεστον εἰς θεοπτίαν, ὑπεμφαίνειν ἔοικεν, τὸ βλέπειν ἀεὶ τὰ Χερουβὶμ ἐπὶ τὸ ἱλαστήριον. Ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ δὲ σχήματι γράφει τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ ὁ προφήτης Ἡσαΐας, λέγων· «Εἶδον τὸν Κύριον Σαβαὼθ καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου ὑψηλοῦ καὶ ἐπηρμένου, καὶ Σεραφὶμ εἱστήκεσαν κύκλῳ αὐτοῦ,» καὶ ἓξ μὲν ἑκάστῳ πτέρυγας ἐκπεφυκέναι, φησὶ, καλύπτειν δὲ αὐτὰ, ταῖς μὲν δυσὶ τοὺς πόδας, ταῖς δὲ δυσὶ τὰ πρόσωπα, πέτεσθαι δὲ ταῖς ἑτέραις. Καὶ εἰ μὲν οἴοιτό τις ὅτι τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόσωπον, καὶ μὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας κατεκάλυπτον τὰ Σεραφὶμ, οὐδὲν ἀπεικὸς ἐννοεῖν τι τοιοῦτον. Μετατρέποντες γὰρ εἰς Ἑλλήνων φωνὴν, τοῦ Σεραφὶμ τὴν δήλωσιν, γνώσεως πληθυσμὸν ἤτοι σοφίας χύσιν σημαινομένην εὑρήσομεν. Ὑπεμφαίνουσι τοιγαροῦν τῷ σχήματι καὶ μάλα σαφῶς, αἱ πάνσοφοί τε καὶ ἀνωτάτω δυνάμεις, ὅτι Θεοῦ πρόσωπον οὐ θέμις ὁρᾶσθαι πρός τινος. Ἄποπτος γὰρ παντελῶς ἡ ὑπὲρ πάντα νοῦν ἐστι φύσις, καὶ φῶς ἀπρόσιτον οἰκεῖ, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνὴν, καὶ «Οὐδεὶς ὄψεται Θεοῦ πρόσωπον, καὶ ζήσεται,» κατά γε τὸ παρ' αὐτοῦ πρὸς Μωσέα τὸν ἱερώτατον εἰρημένον ὀρθῶς. Ἀλλ' οὐδ' ἄν τις γνοίη τά τε ἴχνη καὶ τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ. Γέγραπται γὰρ, «Ὦ βάθος πλούτου, καὶ σοφίας, καὶ γνώσεως Θεοῦ· ὡς ἀνεξερεύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ!» Ψάλλει δὲ καὶ ὁ μακάριος Δαβὶδ, καὶ σοφὸν ἀνακρούει μέλος· «Ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἡ ὁδός σου, καὶ αἱ τρίβοι σου ἐν ὕδασι πολλοῖς, καὶ τὰ ἴχνη σου οὐ γνωσθήσονται.» Ὥσπερ γὰρ οὐκ ἄν τις ἴδοι ἴχνος ἐν ὕδασιν, ἢ ἀνθρώπου τυχὸν ἢ νεὼς, ἢ τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς νηχομένων, οὕτως οὐκ ἂν καταθρήσειέ τις θείας τε καὶ ἀποῤῥήτους ὁδούς. Ὧν ἂν εἶεν εἰς τύπον οἱ πόδες. Εἰ δὲ δὴ καὶ τὰ ἑαυτῶν πρόσωπα καὶ τοὺς πόδας καταπυκάζειν ταῖς πτέρυξιν ὑποτοπήσαιτό τις τὰ ἅγια Σεραφὶμ, ἐννοῶμεν ὅτι τῆς περὶ Θεοῦ σοφίας, ἤτοι γνώσεως ἀρχὴν ἢ τέλος ἰδεῖν οὐ θέμις. Ἀκατάληπτος γὰρ καὶ αὐτὴ, καὶ ὑπὲρ νοῦν ἐστι τὸν ἀνθρώπινον. Ἀρχὴ δὲ παντὸς σώματος, κεφαλή· τέλος δὲ οἱ πόδες. Τὸ ἱλαστήριον οὖν ἄρα Χριστὸς, ὃς καὶ ἐν σαρκὶ πεφηνὼς, οὐδὲν ἧττόν ἐστι Θεὸς, καὶ Κύριος, φύσει τε καὶ ἀληθῶς, περιεστώσας ἐν κύκλῳ δουλοπρεπῶς καὶ αὐτὰς ἔχων τὰς ἀνωτάτω δυνάμεις. Ἔφη δέ που καὶ λόγος ἡμῖν ἱερὸς, ὡς μετά γε τὸ ἐκστῆναι τὸν Σατανᾶν τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ μεθέντα πεῖραν, ὅτε νενήστευκεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ· «Πνεύματα γάρ εἰσι λει
pass_a_gloss: [cont. John 14:6 from s7: 'No one comes to the] Father except through me.' Yet even if the only-begotten Word of God (ὁ μονογενὴς τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος) became according to us (καθ' ἡμᾶς), lowering (καθίημι) himself into humanity (ἀνθρωπότης) and emptying (κένωσις), still it is his own by nature (ἴδιον φυσικῶς) to be conceived in God-befitting glory (δόξα θεοπρεπής) and to exist in superiorities above creation (ὑπεροχαὶ ὑπὲρ τὴν κτίσιν), just as before the flesh. Therefore the cherubim stand around (περιίστημι) the mercy seat, covering (πυκάζω) with wings, turned toward it, always pressing/fixing the face on it (ἐπερείδω); and a clear proof (ἀπόδειξις ἐναργής) of bodyguard-escort (δορυφορία) is the standing to right and left. The always-looking of the cherubim on the mercy seat seems to hint (ὑπεμφαίνω) at the intent and insatiable (ἔντονον, ἀκόρεστον) [disposition] of the highest powers (ἀνώτατοι δυνάμεις) toward God-seeing (θεοπτία). In his own/proper form (ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ σχήματι) Isaiah the prophet writes the Son: 'I saw the Lord Sabaoth sitting on a throne high and lifted up, and seraphim stood around him'; and six wings grew (ἐκφύω) on each, and they covered (καλύπτω) with two the feet, with two the faces, and flew with the others. If someone thinks the seraphim covered the face of God and his feet, nothing unlikely (ἀπεικός) in conceiving so. For turning into the Greeks' tongue the meaning (δήλωσις) of 'Seraphim', we will find it signifies multitude of knowledge (γνώσεως πληθυσμός) or pouring of wisdom (σοφίας χύσις). So by the posture (σχῆμα) the all-wise and highest powers hint very clearly that it is not lawful (οὐ θέμις) for God's face to be seen by anyone. For the nature beyond all mind is wholly invisible (ἄποπτος), and dwells in unapproachable light (φῶς ἀπρόσιτον), per blessed Paul; and 'No one will see God's face and live,' as was rightly said by him [God] to the most holy Moses. Nor could one know his tracks and ways (ἴχνη, ὁδοί). Written: 'O depth of riches and wisdom and knowledge of God; how unsearchable (ἀνεξερεύνητα) his judgments and untraceable (ἀνεξιχνίαστοι) his ways!' David sings, striking up (ἀνακρούω) a wise song (μέλος): 'In the sea your way, your paths in many waters, and your tracks will not be known.' As one could not see a track in waters, of man or ship (ναῦς) or swimmers, so no one could discern (καταθρέω) the divine and ineffable (ἀπόρρητοι) ways; of which the feet would be a type. If one suppose the holy seraphim cover their own faces and feet with their wings, let us conceive that of the wisdom or knowledge about God it is not lawful to see beginning or end (ἀρχή, τέλος). For it too is incomprehensible (ἀκατάληπτος) and beyond human mind. Beginning of every body the head, end the feet. So the mercy seat is Christ, who even having appeared in flesh (ἐν σαρκὶ πεφηνώς) is no less God and Lord by nature and truly (φύσει τε καὶ ἀληθῶς), having even the highest powers standing around in a circle servant-wise (δουλοπρεπῶς). A sacred word (λόγος ἱερός) says that after Satan stood off (ἐξίστημι), having let go the trial (πεῖρα) on Christ, when he had fasted for us (ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν), angels came and served (διακονέω) him: 'For they are ministe[ring] spirits' [cont. in s9].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …Father except through me’ (John 14:6). Yet even though the only-begotten Word of God became like us, lowering himself into humanity and self-emptying (Philippians 2:7), it still belongs to him by nature to be thought of in the glory that befits God and to exist in the heights that are above creation, just as he did, of course, before the flesh. That is why the cherubim stand around the mercy seat, covering it with their wings, turned toward it and always keeping their faces fixed on it (Exodus 25:20); and their station on the right and on the left is a clear proof that they are its guard of honor. And the fact that the cherubim always look toward the mercy seat seems to hint at how intent, and, as it were, insatiable, the highest powers are in beholding God.

The prophet Isaiah, too, portrays the Son in the form proper to him, saying, ‘I saw the Lord of hosts sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and seraphim stood around him’ (Isaiah 6:1–2); and he says that six wings had grown on each, and that with two they covered the feet, with two the faces, and with the others they flew (Isaiah 6:2). If someone thinks that the seraphim were covering the face of God, and his feet too, there is nothing unreasonable in taking it so. For if we put the meaning of the word ‘seraphim’ into Greek, we shall find that it signifies a fullness of knowledge, or an outpouring of wisdom. By their posture, then, these all-wise and highest powers hint very clearly that it is not lawful for God’s face to be seen by anyone. For the nature that is beyond all understanding is wholly beyond sight, and ‘dwells in unapproachable light’ (1 Timothy 6:16), in the words of blessed Paul; and ‘no one shall see the face of God and live’ (Exodus 33:20), as God rightly told the most holy Moses. Nor could anyone know his footsteps and his ways. For it is written, ‘O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable his ways!’ (Romans 11:33) Blessed David, too, sings and strikes up a wise song: ‘Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters, and your footsteps will not be known’ (Psalm 77:19). For just as no one could see a track in water, whether of a man, perhaps, or of a ship, or of the creatures that swim in it, so no one could make out the divine and ineffable ways. The feet would be a type of these ways.

But if someone should suppose that the holy seraphim cover their own faces and feet with their wings, let us understand that it is not lawful to see the beginning or the end of the wisdom, or knowledge, that concerns God. For it too is beyond grasp, and beyond the human mind. The beginning of every body is the head, and its end the feet. So the mercy seat is Christ, who, even when he appeared in the flesh, is no less God and Lord, by nature and in truth, and has even the highest powers standing around him in a circle as servants. And the sacred word also tells us somewhere that after Satan withdrew, giving up his testing of Christ when he had fasted for us, angels came and served him (Matthew 4:11). For ‘they are ministering spirits…

choices.why: Isaiah 6:1: Cyril's 'Κύριον Σαβαώθ' adds Sabaoth (from 6:3, 6:5) to LXX 6:1; rendered 'the Lord of hosts'.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-quotation of John 14:6 begun at the end of s7. It ends mid-word inside Hebrews 1:14 ('Πνεύματα γάρ εἰσι λει | τουργικά'): the English stops at 'For ‘they are ministering spirits' and the quotation closes in s9, which must carry the inline citation (Hebrews 1:14); it is not cited here so that no citation sits inside an open quotation. Psalm 77:19 = LXX Psalm 76:20 (Hebrew 77:20). Isaiah 6:1: Cyril's 'Κύριον Σαβαώθ' adds Sabaoth (from 6:3, 6:5) to LXX 6:1; rendered 'the Lord of hosts'. Isaiah 6:2 LXX lacks a possessive with 'the face' and 'the feet', which is why Cyril can weigh whether the seraphim cover God's face and feet or their own; the English keeps 'the feet', 'the faces' without a possessive for that reason. Cyril gives the feet first, then the faces; order kept. The etymology 'fullness of knowledge' is the one Philo and later writers give for 'cherubim'; Cyril applies it, with 'outpouring of wisdom', to 'seraphim'. Translated as he has it, without correction. ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ σχήματι taken as 'in the form proper to him' (the Son in his own divine glory, matching the preceding point), not 'in the same posture'. 'As God rightly told the most holy Moses' replaces the pronoun παρ' αὐτοῦ with 'God' so readers do not take it as Paul; no concept added. ἄποπτος rendered 'beyond sight'. κένωσις: clear allusion to Philippians 2:7 ('emptied himself'), cited. Exodus 25:20 cited for the cherubim facing and covering the mercy seat (Cyril's paraphrase of the passage quoted in s7). The untraceable ship's track may recall Wisdom 5:10 or Proverbs 30:19; doubtful, uncited. 'Appeared in the flesh' (ἐν σαρκὶ πεφηνώς) may echo 1 Timothy 3:16 (ἐφανερώθη ἐν σαρκί), but the verb differs; uncited. 'Beyond all understanding' may echo Philippians 4:7; uncited.

changes: Gerund 'the cherubim's always looking' recast; ἀκόρεστον 'insatiable'; θεοπτία 'beholding God'
'Of these the feet would be a type' -> 'The feet would be a type of these ways' (natural order)
